channel.title: Stapledon's Voyage news
channel.description: Releases and progress on Stapledon's Voyage, a hard-SF game in Godot 4 and AILANG.

item.title: Around a black hole, beside Saturn
item.description: Two new videos show recent work in motion: a stable orbit around Sagittarius A* and the guided voyage arriving beside Saturn. Both are captures of the game, with the AILANG simulation supplying the motion, clocks and arrival state.
item.content:encoded:
Two new videos show recent work in motion: a stable orbit around Sagittarius A* and the guided voyage arriving beside Saturn. Both are captures of the game, with the AILANG simulation supplying the motion, clocks and arrival state.

Around Sagittarius A*​

The ship completes more than one orbit at three horizon radii. Gravitational lensing bends the background around the shadow while the native HUD shows the orbit count, clock rates and tidal load. This 20-second clip advances 1,800 seconds on the ship's clock, explicitly labelled as 90× presentation speed.

The background is the labelled Sol sky. A true Galactic-Centre background and a rotating black hole remain future work.

Arriving beside Saturn​

Saturn and its rings grow through the final approach, followed by six seconds at a genuine, stationary arrival. The video's 16-second approach compresses 25 seconds of simulation time; earlier guided stops are omitted. The camera widens its lens near arrival to keep the close planet and rings readable.

The space between stars​

Local interstellar clouds and dust have landed in PR #199. Routes cross source-based local cloud boundaries, the bubble wall responds to the medium, and individual grain impacts have an afterglow. The HUD and Archive explain the densities, assumptions and displayed impact statistics.

This 24-second preview follows six ordered intervals on the real route toward Aldebaran at 0.999c: LIC, Aur, LIC again, hot gas, Hyades and hot gas again. Cuts omit the long stretches between boundaries; each displayed dust tick is 1/30 of a ship second. The tan glow in the warm clouds and darker hot gas show the same renderer responding to different media. Dust emission and afterglow are labelled game approximations.

The source comparisons, rendered defaults and representative performance checks have passed review, along with the complete local and matching CI gates. Free navigation also starts at rest, keeps its system list stable, preserves Earth after arrival and uses unmodified mouse look by default. The separate dense-cloud dataset has unresolved scientific comparisons and is deferred. The remaining first-journey audit also stays on the roadmap.

Watch the videos and browse the captures in the gallery, or see the current roadmap.

item.title: The bridge is where you decide
item.description: Clocks, speed and distance stay visible as you travel. Course plotting and journey commitments now live at the bridge consoles, while M opens a read-only star chart wherever you are.
item.content:encoded:
Clocks, speed and distance stay visible as you travel. Course plotting and journey commitments now live at the bridge consoles, while M opens a read-only star chart wherever you are.

What's new​

  • A quieter HUD. Both clocks share the status strip with your speed, phase and distance. Transit, arrival and gravity cards appear when relevant and keep the central outlook clear. PR #193.
  • Decisions at the consoles. Plot and commit at the navigation station, start a guided voyage at the Voyage console, and read the physics codex at the Archive terminal. Walk there, click to walk, or use the keyboard's Walk-to list; a press-twice confirmation option accompanies the hold. PR #195.
  • A chart you can open anywhere. M shows the neighbourhood without planning, committing or pausing. Tour pause and skip controls stay instant; the decisions have no countdown. PR #195.
  • Sizes for more stars. Catalogue stars without measured radii now get estimates from their brightness, distance and temperature, labelled as inferred. Barnard's Star becomes a visible disc at its stop. Body cards also explain synchronous orbits, including when no such orbit is possible. PR #194.

Not yet​

The first-journey slice still needs its complete console-based playthrough audit and remaining visual acceptance gates. Real interstellar clouds and individual dust impacts are being built on a separate branch and still await validation and render review.

This is a progress update between releases. See the new captures in the gallery.

item.title: Visit Sgr A*: v0.4.0-dev.23 and dev.24
item.description: The black-hole milestone is done: you can fly to the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Galaxy, hover above it and orbit it, with general relativity in the physics and in the picture.
item.content:encoded:
The black-hole milestone is done: you can fly to the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Galaxy, hover above it and orbit it, with general relativity in the physics and in the picture.

Sgr A* aboard the ship​

Choose "Sgr A* (black hole)" in navigation. The ship approaches from 1.3 light years, then hovers at 10, 5 and 3 Schwarzschild radii and orbits at 3. The HUD reads the simulation:

  • Clocks. At 10 r_s, 1 ship-hour is 1.054 home hours; in orbit at 3 r_s it is 1.41. The time you spend near the hole really accumulates on both clocks.
  • Light. It shows the shadow's size and the blueshift of incoming light.
  • Forces. It shows the tide across the bubble, and the hover thrust, which the crew never feels.

Built package-first​

  • The maths. sunholo/relativity 0.10.0 adds a geodesic integrator, cross-checked against the exact solution to 3e-13.
  • The lens tables. They are generated on the AILANG VM and pinned.
  • The shader. A GPU shader mirrors the CPU reference pixel for pixel.
  • The checks. The shadow matches Synge's formula to within 0.01 px at 10, 5 and 3 r_s, and a star directly behind the hole makes an Einstein ring at the predicted angle. R1's black-hole requirements are met.

Also​

  • A light-speed loading screen. Picking a menu option accelerates the real sky to 0.99999c, where it collapses into a point, then a white-out into the ship. Loading itself is 3 to 4 times faster.
  • A Main menu button on the galaxy map.
  • dev.24 fixes dev.23. The exported app was missing the lens tables, so the hole was invisible. Publishing now checks them inside the exported app.

Releases: v0.4.0-dev.23-black-hole, v0.4.0-dev.24-lens-fix · Gallery.

item.title: Stops that show scale, and the way home: v0.4.0-dev.25
item.description: Wherever you stop, the size of what you see now tells you how big it really is. Sol is back on the map, and you can hop between the bodies of a system yourself.
item.content:encoded:
Wherever you stop, the size of what you see now tells you how big it really is. Sol is back on the map, and you can hop between the bodies of a system yourself.

Stops that show relative size​

Every stop used to show a planet at the same 60°, and every star from 1,000 AU as a point. Now apparent size grows with true size, on smooth curves that never put the ship inside anything:

  • Planets and moons. The Moon is 16°, Earth 30° and Jupiter 84°; Saturn's stop clears its main rings.
  • Stars, in free navigation. TRAPPIST-1 is 3.5°, α Centauri A 11° and Aldebaran 61°. Stars with a measured radius get the rule now, and every other star will follow once the package can infer sizes from catalogue data.

Home, and in-system​

  • Sol. It is clickable on the map, and Return to Sol arrives beside Earth.
  • In this system. A list offers every planet, moon and star of the system you are in, and refuses legs that are physically impossible (through Jupiter), saying why.
  • When stopped. The HUD shows where you are, where you came from and how far from Earth.
  • The I key. It now works on the star you have stopped at.
  • Auto view. It is the default, and the game remembers your choice.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.25-free-nav · Gallery.

item.title: Back to 60 fps, and inspect what you orbit: v0.4.0-dev.21
item.description: dev.20's full sky made the laptop stutter at Aldebaran. One line was scanning all 335,189 stars every frame. Fixed, measured on the MacBook Air, and the I key now shows the bodies around you.
item.content:encoded:
dev.20's full sky made the laptop stutter at Aldebaran. One line was scanning all 335,189 stars every frame. Fixed, measured on the MacBook Air, and the I key now shows the bodies around you.

The lag​

A performance audit on the M2 Air at the Aldebaran stop showed 53 fps, and 30 fps in the overview. Switching suspects off one at a time on the Studio cleared the new ship lighting and pointed at the 100 pc sky. Timing the per-frame calls found it: a check that ran every frame compared each nearby star against all 335,189 star identities, one by one, before deciding nothing had changed. That took 13.7 ms of a 16.7 ms frame. With a hash lookup it takes 0.01 ms.

On the Air, the same stop now runs at 60 fps at the median in every view, the overview included, with no frame over 25 ms. A regression test fails if this cost ever grows with the number of stars again.

Hold I​

Holding I used to ring only background stars. Now it also rings the Sun, planets, moons, finite stars and exoplanets, at the size they are drawn, aberration included. Click one for its card: distance, size and apparent size, temperature, how long ago its light left, and its data source.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.21-perf-inspect · Gallery · PRs #155, #156.

item.title: A title screen, and a first look at a black hole: v0.4.0-dev.22
item.description: The game now opens on a menu. Meanwhile the black-hole milestone is two-thirds built: the first renders of Sgr A*'s lensed sky are in, checked against general relativity to a fraction of a pixel.
item.content:encoded:
The game now opens on a menu. Meanwhile the black-hole milestone is two-thirds built: the first renders of Sgr A*'s lensed sky are in, checked against general relativity to a fraction of a pixel.

The title screen​

A double-click opens a menu over the real Milky Way: Board the ship, the Guided voyage, the Galaxy map, Settings (Realistic or Auto view, text-only AI) and Credits, read from the repository's own citations. Esc in the ship returns to it.

Black holes (in progress)​

M3 brings general relativity:

  • The maths is in the package first. sunholo/relativity 0.10.0 adds a geodesic integrator, cross-checked against the exact solution to 3e-13.
  • The sim reports what you would feel. Clock rates, tides across the bubble, and the thrust to hover, all at Sgr A*.
  • A GPU shader bends the sky. It reads lens tables generated on the AILANG VM.

The shadow matches Synge's formula to within 0.01 px at 10, 5 and 3 r_s. A star directly behind the hole becomes an Einstein ring at the predicted angle; just off-axis, it splits into two images.

The playable trip is next: hover at 10, 5 and 3 r_s, then orbit, from the bridge. The HUD reads the sim, so "1 ship-hour = 1.41 home hours" in orbit at 3 r_s.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.22-title-screen · Gallery.

item.title: Stars with real size: v0.4.0-dev.19
item.description: Until now only the Sun and α Centauri had a size; every other star you visited was a point seen from 1,000 AU away. Now each star in the voyage is a real disc with its measured radius and temperature, and you arrive where its size means something.
item.content:encoded:
Until now only the Sun and α Centauri had a size; every other star you visited was a point seen from 1,000 AU away. Now each star in the voyage is a real disc with its measured radius and temperature, and you arrive where its size means something.

What's new​

  • Aldebaran (45 solar radii, 3,927 K) and TRAPPIST-1 (0.119 solar radii, 2,566 K) are finite stars with cited measurements, in place of catalogue points.
  • One stop rule. Main-sequence stars stop in their habitable zone, where they look like the Sun from Earth: α Cen A at 1.233 AU, about half a degree; TRAPPIST-1 at 0.0235 AU, a deep-orange disc 2.7° across beside where its planets orbit. Giants stop where they fill 40° of sky: Aldebaran from 0.615 AU.
  • The same rhythm everywhere. Each star's final hop is 30 s accelerating, about a minute cruising, then the 25 s final approach, like the planets.

Not yet​

Aldebaran is so bright at 40° that it reads white; dimmed, it is pale orange. Its approach is still relativistic, since it is already 4° across six AU out. Both are open questions. TRAPPIST-1's seven planets are next.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.19-finite-stars · Gallery · Integration PR #139.

item.title: Real exoplanets, real starlight: v0.4.0-dev.20
item.description: The voyage now reaches a real planetary system, the ship is lit by whichever star it is near, and the sky holds six times more stars, each in exactly one place.
item.content:encoded:
The voyage now reaches a real planetary system, the ship is lit by whichever star it is near, and the sky holds six times more stars, each in exactly one place.

What's new​

  • TRAPPIST-1's seven planets. At the habitable-zone stop, planets b–h are where they really are when you arrive. Sizes and orbits come from Agol et al. 2021, positions from transit timings (Ducrot et al. 2020) corrected for 40.6 years of light travel. Planet e is 0.72° across, bigger than our Moon; c is a crescent and d half lit. Albedos and surfaces are assumed and labelled so.
  • The ship lit by the real star. The bridge's key light comes from the Sun, or the star you are visiting, as seen through the bubble: its direction (aberration included), its colour (Doppler included) and a log-compressed brightness, labelled as not physical. Sun shadows sweep the deck as the ship turns; TRAPPIST-1 is a dim red glow; Aldebaran floods the deck with warm light. Deep space hands back to the ship's own lighting.
  • Star colours (D-49). Auto view dims a star just enough to keep its hue and lifts its blackbody colour: Aldebaran golden orange, TRAPPIST-1 an ember. Realistic view is unchanged.
  • A giant's approach. Aldebaran's final approach lasts 90 s, so the giant grows out of the starbow, blue-white at first from your own speed, turning golden as you stop.
  • One position per star. Navigation and the sky now read a single truth table built in AILANG. Before, a map journey could arrive with the star drawn up to 8.7 ly away; now it's always ahead.
  • The full 100 pc sky. 331,311 nearby stars from Gaia instead of about 50,000, for about 0.3 ms a frame.

Not yet​

You can't fly to a TRAPPIST-1 planet yet, because its surface would have to be invented. The 100 pc sky's cost on a MacBook Air is an estimate (+1.3–1.8 ms) until measured.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.20-trappist-planets · Gallery · PRs #143, #146, #149.

item.title: Even legs and a gentle arrival: v0.4.0-dev.18
item.description: Every Solar System leg now has the same rhythm, about 2¼ minutes in real time: 30 seconds accelerating, about a minute cruising, then braking into a 25-second final approach. The longer legs simply go faster, above 0.999c to Jupiter and Saturn, so the planets now ease into view instead of appearing in the last few seconds.
item.content:encoded:
Every Solar System leg now has the same rhythm, about 2¼ minutes in real time: 30 seconds accelerating, about a minute cruising, then braking into a 25-second final approach. The longer legs simply go faster, above 0.999c to Jupiter and Saturn, so the planets now ease into view instead of appearing in the last few seconds.

What's new​

  • Even legs. The simulation solves each leg's thrust and cruise speed so the boost lasts 30 s and the cruise about 60 s: 0.07c for the short Callisto hop, 0.99943c (γ 30) to Jupiter, 0.99963c (γ 37) to Saturn. Sun → Jupiter takes about 2¼ minutes instead of 6½.
  • A gentle final approach. A new trip profile brakes hard, then eases in for 25 s from where the planet is 4° across, so Jupiter grows smoothly instead of exploding in the last 8 s. It's built from the same exact constant-acceleration physics, in sunholo/relativity 0.9.0. The HUD says FINAL APPROACH.
  • Skip stage [K]. Jump to the next stage of the leg: accelerating → cruise → braking → final approach → arrival. It lands exactly on each stage, and the HUD counts how many you skipped.
  • Distances on the HUD: to the destination, from the last stop, and from Earth, plus this leg's thrust.

Not yet​

At the faster in-system speeds, the bubble wall's glow tints the forward view; how to present it is open. Stars beyond the Sun still appear as points: giving every visited star its real size (TRAPPIST-1, Aldebaran) is the next sprint.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.18-even-legs · Gallery · Integration PR #134.

item.title: A real-time voyage to Aldebaran: v0.4.0-dev.17
item.description: The guided tour no longer fast-forwards. Every boost and every braking plays at one ship second per wall second, and special relativity, not a time-lapse, is what makes the trips short. Earth to Jupiter takes six minutes aboard while 39 pass on Earth. Then the voyage leaves the Sun behind: α Centauri, TRAPPIST-1 and Aldebaran, 120 Earth years later.
item.content:encoded:
The guided tour no longer fast-forwards. Every boost and every braking plays at one ship second per wall second, and special relativity, not a time-lapse, is what makes the trips short. Earth to Jupiter takes six minutes aboard while 39 pass on Earth. Then the voyage leaves the Sun behind: α Centauri, TRAPPIST-1 and Aldebaran, 120 Earth years later.

What's new​

  • Real time, no compression. A single drive (3,000,000 g, inertia-damped as the bubble's fiction allows) takes the Solar System legs to 0.99c. You watch the starbow form during each 27-second boost and unwind during braking. Both clocks are on the HUD, and they drift apart in front of you.
  • Further and faster. α Centauri at 0.999c, then TRAPPIST-1 at 0.9999c, then Aldebaran, 66.6 light-years away, at 0.999999c (γ 707). The whole voyage is about 11 months aboard and 120 years at home.
  • Cruise interludes. Interstellar cruises are long: 70, 216 and 38 days aboard. After the boost and ten seconds of cruise, the game hands over to an interlude. Today it is a card that states speed, γ, both clocks, how old news from home is, and what the elapsed Earth time means. In the full game the interlude is where life aboard happens. Braking into each star plays in real time.
  • Stars where you arrive. Two star catalogues disagreed about where some stars are, by up to thousands of AU, which only shows when you stop 1,000 AU away. Destinations now render exactly where the simulation flies.
  • A compact HUD: where you're going, the phase, the speed (from the simulation's exact 1 − β), γ, km/s and both clocks. The details are behind Tab.

Not yet​

TRAPPIST-1's seven planets are planned as a real stop; for now you arrive at the star. At the highest speeds the glowing bubble wall washes out the forward view; how to present that is an open design question. Ship lighting still doesn't follow the Sun.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.17-real-time-voyage · Gallery · Integration PR #130.

item.title: Manual sky exposure and a one-AU arrival: v0.4.0-dev.14
item.description: The painted ship and Solar departure tour share one perspective. This review build removes automatic sky dimming: exposure stays at your manually selected brightness while you move and look around. The tour finishes one AU from Alpha Centauri A.
item.content:encoded:
The painted ship and Solar departure tour share one perspective. This review build removes automatic sky dimming: exposure stays at your manually selected brightness while you move and look around. The tour finishes one AU from Alpha Centauri A.

Development build: macOS only (Apple Silicon)v0.4.0-dev.14-manual-sky

Painted ship and Solar departure tour

Download for macOS

Pre-alpha and unsigned. After unzipping, clear the quarantine flag once:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "Stapledons Voyage.app"

What's new​

  • One current painted ship: seven major tiers, a bridge floor and captain shadow that meet the walking surface, faster movement, trackpad look and known-star inspection. Integration PR.
  • Gradual approaches: the guided tour uses physical 1 g acceleration with 90 seconds of braking playback. Earth, Jupiter and Saturn sit beside the bridge at their close stops. Ordinary navigation keeps its existing pacing. Integration PR.
  • Manual sky exposure: J cycles the brightness settings, also available under Tab. Bright planets and suns can wash out at a setting chosen for stars; camera pans and journeys no longer change exposure automatically. The physical light and SR calculations remain unchanged.
  • Smoother tour starts: initialize the camera from the new session and ease departure time compression over three seconds. This corrects an initial camera jump and an abrupt first movement beside Earth.
  • Measured stars: Alpha Centauri A/B use measured radii and temperatures; the final leg intercepts the moving primary at 1 AU. A's disc is about 0.65° wide there. Integration PR.
  • Review evidence: the gallery and geometry reference include fresh native captures and editable Blender masters. B keeps the full benchmark locally and attempts an authenticated upload of filtered aggregate measurements. Integration PR.

Not yet​

Ship lighting is still an internal lighting study; external sunlight, detailed moon surfaces and further Commons art remain in progress. Fresh M2 Air performance needs a laptop measurement. Tour stops are inertial clearance stops: gravity, thermal hazards and GR are not simulated. Stellar photospheres are uniform emitters.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.14-manual-sky · Gallery · Ship reference.

item.title: Walkable bridge demo: v0.4.0-dev.1
item.description: A development build you can download: walk the captain around the bridge under the live
item.content:encoded:
A development build you can download: walk the captain around the bridge under the live relativistic sky, open the galaxy map from the nav console, and fly a journey to α Centauri A through the bubble. macOS only, Apple Silicon.

Development build: macOS only (Apple Silicon)v0.4.0-dev.14-manual-sky

Painted ship and Solar departure tour

Download for macOS

Pre-alpha and unsigned. After unzipping, clear the quarantine flag once:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "Stapledons Voyage.app"

What's new​

  • The walkable bridge (M4.2, #102): the bridge disc at the top of the spire, composited with the live sky through the same camera. The captain walks it (WASD, E to use) and ages with ship time.
  • Navigation from the bridge: a nav console opens the galaxy map (M), built from the real catalogues: 5,685 stars within 25 pc, companions at their system's distance. Commit to α Centauri A and watch the boost, the 0.99c cruise, the brake and the arrival.
  • The relativistic sky behind it all: 335k real stars, aberration and Doppler colour, the naked-eye exposure, and the forward glow of the cosmic background at extreme speed.
  • L opens the log and K the codex.

Not yet​

  • The forward bubble-wall glow is off; it returns with the next simulation step.
  • The standalone sky flight (-- --voyage) shows a mirrored sky in this build: fixed on main (#107), in the next build. The view from the bridge is correct.
  • The bridge is v1 demo art; the final art is in progress (concept art).
  • Pre-alpha and unsigned; see Try it for install notes.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.1 (macOS development build)

item.title: Concept art: the captain and the bridge
item.description: The ship has faces now. The captain is picked, the crew have proposed portraits, and the bridge
item.content:encoded:
The ship has faces now. The captain is picked, the crew have proposed portraits, and the bridge stands in the engine over the live sky.

What's new​

  • The captain, the Longline Navigator (#98): picked from three silhouette proposals, and drawn front and back at 30, 50, 70 and 90, because the game spans a 100-year career.
  • Crew cast proposals: one portrait per role, next to the Medic's accepted set.
  • Bridge v1 (#97, demo art): the first real interior, a disc at the top of the spire inside the sphere ship. The sky behind the railings is not painted; it is the game's live sky, through the same camera, so at 0.99c it crowds forward and turns blue.

Not yet​

Bridge v1 is demo art. A v2 quality study is done and the final art is being made. Everything is on the concept art page, labelled with its status.

item.title: Planets are coming
item.description: A new milestone, M5, brings planets, moons and flybys inside a star system, with the same rule as
item.content:encoded:
A new milestone, M5, brings planets, moons and flybys inside a star system, with the same rule as the sky: real data, real physics.

What's done​

  • The design and the sprint plan are approved (#84, #86).
  • A new AILANG package, sunholo/celestial 0.1.0, published with 93 tests: a Kepler solver, JPL planetary ephemerides for 3000 BC to 3000 AD plus moons, IAU reference frames, light-time, gravity, reflectance, and planetary rings.
  • sunholo/relativity 0.6 and 0.7: the bubble's forward glow, and the aberrated outline of a nearby sphere, which is what a planet looks like as you pass it near light speed.

What's planned​

Start held above Earth, pick a body on a system map (the Sun, 8 planets, 11 moons, 4 ring systems), choose to stop or fly by at 0.001c to 0.99c, commit, and ride the leg. The views will be exact: light-time delay, aberration, and the Terrell rotation that makes a passing sphere look turned. At α Centauri, the known and candidate planets will show as points only, with a badge saying how sure the astronomy is. The first step, the Sol and α Cen data and the game's package pins, has merged (#99).

See the roadmap.

item.title: The ship's AI foundation
item.description: The crew's optional AI layer runs end to end, so far on a deterministic test stub: lines with
item.content:encoded:
The crew's optional AI layer runs end to end, so far on a deterministic test stub: lines with emotion markers, portraits that change with them, a voice, and a hard cost ceiling.

What's new​

  • Emotion markers (AI.1–AI.3): a line carries markers like {loving}, validated before the game uses it.
  • A service the game never waits on (AI.4–AI.7): provider routing, a cache, a supervised background process, and key hygiene: a key never appears on a command line.
  • The Medic's accepted portraits, pinned and content-addressed (AI.8).
  • Opt-in and capped (AI.9): live AI stays off until the player adds a key and ticks the box. A ceiling the player sets (US$0.50 by default) stops spending, and automated runs can never go live.
  • The conversation scene (AI.10a, #91): the portrait cross-fades as each emotion marker arrives, the subtitles build segment by segment, and the voice plays.

Not yet​

No live model has been called. The first live run (AI.10b) is attended: one real line and a few voice auditions under a US$1 ceiling. The voice in the clip is a placeholder.

item.title: A galaxy map from real catalogues
item.description: The galaxy map now draws from the same star catalogues as the sky, and stars that belong together
item.content:encoded:
The galaxy map now draws from the same star catalogues as the sky, and stars that belong together stay together.

What's new​

  • The map on the catalogue tiers (#81): 5,687 stars within 25 pc, up from 3,802, with full-precision positions. α Centauri A and B are separate stars you can select.
  • Companion stars at their system's distance (#89): a companion within 60″ and 2,000 AU of its primary, agreeing in parallax and proper motion, takes the system's distance rather than its own noisier one. That moved 20,524 companions; Sirius B, for one, now sits with Sirius A at 8.6 ly.

Not yet​

Both are in the walkable bridge demo, v0.4.0-dev.1.

item.title: The relativistic sky
item.description: The sky out of the window is now the real one: 335,157 stars over the Milky Way, exposed for a
item.content:encoded:
The sky out of the window is now the real one: 335,157 stars over the Milky Way, exposed for a dark-adapted human eye, with the cosmic background glowing ahead at extreme speeds.

What's new​

  • Starfield v2 (#67): 335,157 stars from CNS5, Gaia GCNS and Hipparcos, instanced on the GPU, with float64 positions rebased around the ship.
  • The Milky Way behind them: the NOIRLab panorama with the catalogue's own stars removed, so stars are not counted twice, Doppler shifted texel by texel.
  • A naked-eye exposure (#75, #80): stars in lux and the sky in cd/m², calibrated so the faintest visible star lands at V 6.9 (Crumey's model says 6.897). The HUD always says how it is exposing; the readability aids are off by default and labelled.
  • The forward CMB glow (#79, fixed in #88): above γ ≈ 150 the 2.7 K microwave background, blueshifted, shows up dead ahead; at γ 707 it is a 3,853.7 K blackbody.

Not yet​

M1's acceptance step (M1.5b) is still open: the reference renders at five speeds and the 60 fps bench at 1440p with everything on. See the roadmap.

item.title: v0.3: plan, commit, transit, arrive
item.description: The journey core is complete: pick a star, commit, watch both clocks run, and arrive. Once you
item.content:encoded:
The journey core is complete: pick a star, commit, watch both clocks run, and arrive. Once you commit, there is no going back.

What's new​

  • Commit: hold for 1.5 s. After that the simulation refuses every cancel, and says so.
  • Transit and arrival: the phase, both clocks, the distance flown and the energy radiated, live, until you arrive.
  • Deterministic replay: a 10,000-tick session replays byte for byte on the AILANG VM and the interpreter.
  • v0.3.1 opens straight onto the galaxy map; v0.3.2 adds trackpad zoom and Retina scaling.

Not yet​

The interior of the ship, and a journey you live through on board, are the next milestone (M4).

Releases: v0.3.0, v0.3.1, v0.3.2 (macOS review builds)

item.title: v0.2.0: a galaxy map with real numbers
item.description: The game now opens on a 3D map of the nearby stars. Click one and the simulation plans the trip:
item.content:encoded:
The game now opens on a 3D map of the nearby stars. Click one and the simulation plans the trip: your years against Earth's.

What's new​

  • A galaxy map of the nearby-star catalogue: drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, click to plan.
  • A cruise slider from 0.9c to 0.999999c, spaced evenly in rapidity, 0.99c by default.
  • Every number on the panel comes straight from the AILANG simulation. α Centauri A at 0.99c: 0.6208 years for you, 4.401 for Earth, 1.80 minutes of boost at each end.

Not yet​

Committing to the journey and flying it came in the next build.

Release: v0.2.0-m2-map (macOS review build)

item.content:encoded:
The first review build: an AILANG simulation driving a Godot starfield, with relativity that is tested rather than eyeballed.

What's new​

  • The simulation runs in AILANG as a child process, talking one line of JSON per tick with Godot (about 50 µs per round trip). It flies the ship at 1 g with exact rapidity kinematics.
  • The starfield: 3,802 nearby stars (CNS5), each aberrated toward the bow, coloured as a Doppler-shifted blackbody and beamed brighter ahead.
  • 27 physics reference checks, and 9 cases where the GPU shader must put a star where the CPU reference says, to under 0.1 px.

Not yet​

No Milky Way behind the stars, one axis of motion, and star colours from the spectral class only. All three were fixed in M1.

Release: v0.1.0-m0 (macOS review build)
